## Photolysis reaction rates and their Jacobian (`PhotoChem`) {#sec-ch07-photochem}

### Summary

`PhotoChem` turns photolysis rate constants into reaction rates and gives the caller the derivative it needs for an
implicit step. Each rate is the rate constant times the reactant concentrations, as in the mass-action law of
@sec-ch06. The stoichiometric matrix comes from the reaction equations, not from the branches. Two further helpers
weight the branches by their share of the rate, or map rates into a species-space Jacobian.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $r_j = J_j \prod_n c_n^{\nu_{nj}}$ and $\partial r_j/\partial c_m$, @eq-ch07-photochem-rate.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $c$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$], $F$; returns $r$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$] per reaction.

**Placement.** Called by the driver once per step, like `Kinetics` (@sec-ch06).

**Activation.** `PhotoChemOptions.from_yaml` on a file with `type: photolysis` reactions; API `PhotoChem`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Concentrations floored at $10^{-300}$; stoichiometry from the equation.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $r_j$, rate of reaction $j$ [$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$]; $c_n$, molar concentration of species $n$
[$\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$] (as in @sec-appa); $\nu_{nj}$, reactant coefficient of species $n$ in reaction $j$ [-]; $f_b$, share of branch
$b$ in the branch-weighted rate [-].

### Derivation

The reaction rate and its reaction-space Jacobian are

$$
\begin{aligned}
r_j &= J_j \prod_n c_n^{\nu_{nj}} ,\\
\frac{\partial r_j}{\partial c_m} &= \nu_{mj}\, \frac{r_j}{c_m} .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch07-photochem-rate}

@eq-ch07-photochem-rate is computed in `forward` and `jacobian`
({{< code src/photochem/photochem.cpp PhotoChemImpl::forward >}},
{{< code src/photochem/photochem.cpp PhotoChemImpl::jacobian >}}). $J_j$ does not depend on $c$, so the Jacobian has no
rate-constant term; it has no temperature term either.

The branch-weighted stoichiometry of one reaction is

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_b &= \frac{\int \sigma_b F\, \mathrm d\lambda}{\sum_{b'} \int \sigma_{b'} F\, \mathrm d\lambda + 10^{-30}} ,\\
\bar s_n &= \sum_b f_b\, s_{bn} ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch07-photochem-effective}

with $s_{bn}$ the composition of branch $b$. @eq-ch07-photochem-effective is computed in `get_effective_stoich`
({{< code src/photochem/photolysis.cpp PhotolysisImpl::get_effective_stoich >}}). The sum over $b'$ includes the
absorption branch 0, whose composition is the reactant. Verified by a run[^ch07-eff-src]: for `O2 => O + O` with the
rows of @sec-ch07-rate, the result is $\bar s = (0.727, 0.545, 0)$ for $(\mathrm{O_2}, \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{O_3})$. Only a
test calls this function; `PhotoChem` does not.

### Numerical method

`reset` ({{< code src/photochem/photochem.cpp PhotoChemImpl::reset >}}) builds `stoich` (products minus reactants of
the equation) and the reactant orders, then creates the `Photolysis` module. `forward` calls `Photolysis.forward`
and multiplies by the floored concentration product; it does not refresh the cross-section cache, so the caller
calls `update_xs_diss_stacked` first. The species-space helper `jacobian_photolysis_species`
({{< code src/photochem/jacobian_photolysis.cpp jacobian_photolysis_species >}}) returns
$\sum_r S_{nr}\, x_r\, \nu_{mr} / c_m$ for an input $x_r$ that its comment calls the rate constant.

The figure of the call order is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

### Limits

Open questions, not tested:

- For a branched reaction, `stoich` comes from the equation. `data/ch4_photolysis.yaml` lists every branch product in
  one equation, so one photolysis event would produce all of them. Whether the branch weights of
  @eq-ch07-photochem-effective should replace `stoich` is a chemistry question.
- `jacobian_photolysis_species` equals $\partial (\mathrm d c_n/\mathrm dt)/\partial c_m$ only if its input is the
  reaction rate $J c$; with the rate constant, as its comment says, the result is too small by a factor $c_m$. The
  only test checks signs.
